predecessors.name: Republic of Afghanistan (Daoud Republic)
predecessors.text: the whole country: the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan, 'Established: 30 April 1978' after the Saur Revolution of 27-28 April 1978

capitals.name: Taloqan, capital in exile of the Islamic State and the Northern Alliance

ledger.x: 1978: the PDPA proclaims the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan at Kabul.
1979: the Soviet 40th Army enters Afghanistan.
1979: the mujahideen war against the government and the Soviets begins.
1987: the Democratic Republic becomes the Republic of Afghanistan.
15 February 1989: the last Soviet troops leave.
28 April 1992: Kabul falls to the mujahideen.
1992: the mujahideen coalition takes the state.
28 April 1992: the Republic of Afghanistan becomes the Islamic State of Afghanistan, with Kabul as capital until 1996.
Late 1994: the Taliban take the south.
September 1996: the southern contest ends in the Taliban capture of Kabul; the front moves north (next event).
27 September 1996: the Taliban take Kabul.
1996: the Islamic State's government withdraws to Taloqan.
September 1996: the Northern Alliance forms against the Taliban.
8 August 1998: the Taliban take Mazar-i-Sharif.
5 September 2000: the Taliban take Taloqan.
2000: the capital in exile moves from Taloqan to Fayzabad (infobox 'Fayzabad (2000-2001)').
13 November 2001: Kabul is retaken.
November 2001: the government returns to Kabul.
December 2001: the Taliban are driven from power.
December 2001: the Taliban-Alliance front ends with the fall of the Taliban regime.
22 December 2001: the Afghan Interim Administration under Hamid Karzai takes office.
19 June 2002: the Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan.
26 January 2004: the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan.
15 August 2021: the Taliban return to power at Kabul.

wars.name: Soviet–Afghan War
wars.outcome: Infobox result 'Afghan mujahideen victory', 25 December 1979 to 15 February 1989.

wars.name: Afghan civil war, 1992-1996 (as told on the Islamic State of Afghanistan page)
wars.outcome: Rabbani's government lost Kabul to the Taliban in September 1996 and withdrew to the north; the Taliban held 'two-thirds of Afghanistan' by the end of 1996.

wars.name: Taliban–Northern Alliance war, 1996-2001
wars.outcome: The Alliance shrank from about 30% of the population (1996) to 'only about 5% of the country' (2001) and returned with Kabul in November 2001.

wars.name: War in Afghanistan (2001-2021)
wars.outcome: In October 2001 'the United States invaded Afghanistan to remove the Taliban from power'; the Taliban regime ended in December 2001; the Islamic Republic fell when 'The Taliban captured the capital city of Kabul on 15 August 2021'.

certainty.note: Judgement: the outer frontier is the modern international boundary and the pages opened discuss no survey or treaty line (the Durand Line is not on them).
The Taliban-Alliance front moved with each offensive (Mazar-i-Sharif 1998, Taloqan 2000) and the pages give only percentages, so the Alliance's edge is soft.
Whole-country outline; the same judgement as for 1978-1995.
